subChunks.title: Design Systems and Shadcn/ui
subChunks.hookHtml: Most production React + Tailwind apps don't build every component from scratch. Understanding how Shadcn/ui works — and why it's designed the way it is — teaches you the entire component-library architecture that underlies nearly every serious codebase you'll join.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Grand Archmage Solomon: "Most students see a component library and ask: 'How do I install it?' The question that reveals mastery is: 'How is it built?' Because once you can read a Shadcn component, you can modify it, extend it, or replace it."

What Shadcn/ui is — and isn't

Shadcn/ui is not a traditional component library you install as a dependency. You run a CLI command and it copies component source code into your project. You own it entirely.

npx shadcn-ui@latest add button
# Creates: components/ui/button.tsx in YOUR project
# You can open it, read it, and change every class.

Architecture: Radix UI (accessible, unstyled primitives) + Tailwind CSS (styling) + CVA (variants) + cn() (merging).

Reading a Shadcn component

const buttonVariants = cva(
  // Base: accessibility, transitions, disabled state all baked in
  'inline-flex items-center justify-center rounded-md text-sm font-medium ring-offset-background transition-colors focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2 disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50',
  {
    variants: {
      variant: {
        default:     'bg-primary text-primary-foreground hover:bg-primary/90',
        destructive: 'bg-destructive text-destructive-foreground hover:bg-destructive/90',
        outline:     'border border-input bg-background hover:bg-accent hover:text-accent-foreground',
        ghost:       'hover:bg-accent hover:text-accent-foreground',
      },
    },
    defaultVariants: { variant: 'default', size: 'default' },
  }
);

CSS variables like bg-primary are defined in globals.css:

:root {
  --primary: 222.2 47.4% 11.2%;
  --primary-foreground: 210 40% 98%;
}
.dark {
  --primary: 210 40% 98%;
  --primary-foreground: 222.2 47.4% 11.2%;
}

When to use Shadcn vs build from scratch

  • Use Shadcn/Radix: Dialog, Select, Dropdown, Toast, Command, Tooltip, Tabs, Accordion — anything with ARIA roles, focus management, or keyboard navigation.
  • Build from scratch: Card, Badge, Divider, Skeleton, Avatar — simple visual components with no interactive behaviour.

The rule: if a component needs role, aria-*, or keyboard event handling to be correct, use a primitive. Don't reinvent focus traps.

Solomon: "When you copy a Shadcn component into your project, you are not accepting a dependency — you are accepting responsibility. Read every line."

storyBeats.text: Solomon opens a slim dark codex. Its spine reads 'Shadcn'. He slides it across the desk.

storyBeats.speaker: Grand Archmage Solomon
storyBeats.text: Shadcn copies source code into your project. You own it. Radix handles the behaviour. Tailwind handles the styling. CVA handles the variants. cn() handles the merging. Once you see that architecture, you can read any modern component library.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a component card with Shadcn-style structure:

  • .card: rounded-lg, border, border-gray-200, bg-white, shadow-sm
  • .card-header: flex, flex-col, space-y-1.5, p-6
  • .card-title: text-2xl, font-semibold, leading-none, tracking-tight, text-gray-900
  • .card-description: text-sm, text-gray-500
  • .card-content: p-6, pt-0
  • .card-footer: flex, items-center, p-6, pt-0, gap-2

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a custom dropdown trigger button from scratch using the Radix/Headless UI pattern in pure HTML. The button must: have a data-state attribute (open/closed), use aria-expanded, and show/hide a menu panel using only Tailwind classes.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain to a colleague why Shadcn/ui copies source code into your project instead of being an installable npm package. What does that design decision enable that a traditional library cannot?

questions.prompt: How does Shadcn/ui differ from a traditional component library like Material UI?
options: Shadcn copies component source code into your project; you own and can modify every class
Shadcn is installed as an npm package and imported with tree-shaking
Shadcn generates components at runtime based on your theme config
Shadcn only works with Next.js and not standard React
questions.answer: Shadcn copies component source code into your project; you own and can modify every class
questions.explanation: Running npx shadcn-ui add button writes components/ui/button.tsx into your repo. There is no runtime dependency. You can change any class, add any variant, or delete any behaviour. This is the entire design philosophy.

questions.prompt: What role does Radix UI play in the Shadcn/ui architecture?
options: Radix provides accessible, unstyled behaviour primitives (focus traps, ARIA, keyboard nav); Tailwind styles them
Radix provides a default visual theme that Shadcn overrides with Tailwind
Radix handles state management for interactive components
Radix is a CSS framework that Shadcn replaces with Tailwind utilities
questions.answer: Radix provides accessible, unstyled behaviour primitives (focus traps, ARIA, keyboard nav); Tailwind styles them
questions.explanation: Radix focuses entirely on correct behaviour — keyboard navigation, focus management, ARIA attributes — without any visual opinion. Shadcn layers Tailwind classes on top. You get correctness for free and style completely.

questions.prompt: You need to customise a Shadcn Button so the primary variant uses your brand colour instead of the default dark theme. What do you change?
options: Update the --primary CSS variable in globals.css
Edit the npm package source in node_modules
Override the button's Tailwind classes with !important in your CSS
Pass a style prop with the colour directly to each Button usage
questions.answer: Update the --primary CSS variable in globals.css
questions.explanation: Shadcn's theming is entirely driven by CSS variables defined in globals.css. Changing --primary to your brand's HSL values updates every component that uses bg-primary simultaneously, with no class changes needed.
